sources.name: London Plan funding health facilities
sources.fact: Current London Plan states developer contributions can fund capital costs of primary/community care growth and references HUDU modelling

sources.name: Draft London Plan 2026 land and infrastructure
sources.fact: Draft July 2026 plan requires appropriate infrastructure including health and locally assessed social infrastructure; draft status retained

sources.name: LBBD neighbourhood growth summary
sources.fact: Council states schools, GP surgeries and health centres need capacity expansion as homes grow and developer contributions are part of delivery

sources.name: LBBD Inclusive Growth infrastructure
sources.fact: Infrastructure Delivery Plan assesses future needs for growth across infrastructure types

examples: Borough pupil forecasts are planning-area evidence, not proof of capacity at the nearest school
School-place developer contribution guidance does not produce a parcel-specific charge without scheme inputs
Health capital strategy identifies infrastructure need but does not prove GP capacity for a specific development
HUDU or contribution models require development-specific population/use assumptions
Healthy New Town evidence is strategic/place-based and not a parcel-level health score
Draft London Plan policy must remain draft context until adopted
Existing planned school/health projects do not prove completion or available places on a candidate date
No social-infrastructure uplift is assigned without scheme-specific capacity/contribution evidence
